what_ai_proposed: A 2-week delivery plan derived from the brief text
what_changed: Replanned to ~1 day in 9 fixed blocks with explicit scope cuts
why_it_mattered: The real constraint came from the stakeholder (recruiter) and was not in the document
what_i_would_teach: AI plans from the documents you give it. Confirm real constraints with people first and feed them in; a plan that ignores them is confident and wrong

what_ai_proposed: Pinned dbt-duckdb==1.9.1 from its training knowledge
what_changed: Re-pinned to versions proven by a clean install
why_it_mattered: The AI-chosen pin was yanked and dragged in an incompatible dbt-core; CI and reviewers would have failed on first run
what_i_would_teach: Never accept a version pin you have not installed in a clean environment; AI version knowledge is stale by design

what_ai_proposed: Late-data rule applied to every incoming row before de-duplication
what_changed: Exact retries are detected by content hash first; only new or changed lines are judged against the restatement window
why_it_mattered: All 52 tests were green, yet 167 harmless re-sent lines were held as late - revenue would have been understated and Finance flooded with false restatements
what_i_would_teach: Green tests prove the rules you wrote, not that the rules are right. Profile the output (counts by reason, by batch) and ask whether each number is believable before you trust a pipeline

what_ai_proposed: Synthetic-data generator that re-generated all files when a new batch was added
what_changed: Per-month seeds; demo mode only writes new batch files; verified by hashing landed files before/after
why_it_mattered: Landing zones must be immutable - otherwise replays and incremental runs silently disagree with what was originally loaded
what_i_would_teach: Treat the landing zone as an append-only log and test that property (hash before/after), even in a PoC

what_ai_proposed: Fixed 1% quarantine threshold for the monitoring warning
what_changed: Anomaly rule: 3x trailing 6-batch average for the same source and at least 0.2%
why_it_mattered: The fixed rule never fired on the real incident (0.4%) - monitoring that cannot see an outage is worse than none because it gives false confidence
what_i_would_teach: Set alert thresholds from observed baselines, then prove the alert fires on a known-bad case before calling it done

what_ai_proposed: AI agent built a whole block and pushed it to the shared repo without explaining or asking
what_changed: Rolled back; working agreement: explain -> agree -> build locally -> verify -> push only on explicit approval
why_it_mattered: The lead must understand and own every change that reaches the shared repo; speed without review produced work I could not explain
what_i_would_teach: Give AI tools speed inside gates: they draft and build locally, a human understands and approves before anything is shared. Same rule I would set for a new engineer
